events.title: The Synod of Sutri
events.shortBlurb: A synod called by the German king Henry III swept away three rival claimants to the papacy and opened the era of reform…
body: On 20 December 1046, at Sutri north of Rome, a synod convened under King Henry III of Germany confronted the scandal of three men claiming the papacy at once — Benedict IX, Sylvester III, and Gregory VI. The synod deposed the rivals, and within days a reforming German bishop was elected as Pope Clement II, who then crowned Henry emperor.

Sutri broke the grip of the Roman noble factions on the papacy and prepared the way for the Gregorian Reform, the great eleventh-century movement to free the Church from lay control and to renew the life of the clergy.
